name: Notebook
tagline: A careful person's planner: ink, pencil, and one highlighter stroke.
mood: Quiet and orderly, like a ruled page kept by someone who ticks boxes and writes small notes in the margin.
rationale: A tool you glance at a hundred times a day should look like something you already know how to read: a checklist on ruled paper. The notebook gives the pane a fixed anatomy: a 3-cell margin for status glyphs, a graphite margin line, a body column, and a right column of margin notes, every row through the same frame. That answers the spacing complaint directly: the gutter is a drawn line, not an accident of padding; sections are separated by exactly one ruled blank; the sha/agent/time notes end on the same cell. The character comes from a restrained set of materials (ink blue structure, pencil-grey notes, a single highlighter stroke on the line the pen is on), never from decoration.
tokenMap: bg: not drawn; the terminal's own background is the paper (the mock page uses warm charcoal / cream). fg: theme key `text` (ink): the title and the count (bold, so the pane's most-read row never depends on a hex), todo step text, the question text and the drift `~`. dim: `dimColor` (pencil): done rows, margin notes, `·` separators, empty meter boxes. accent (ink blue): hex pair `#8db4f0` dark / `#2d55c4` light, for structure that never carries the only copy of information: the `✎` pen, the `▸` current-phase mark, the PLAN/SIGNALS labels, the filled meter boxes and the band's `7/18`; the hooks module reads the `theme` row of `$.config.list()` once per session: a value matching /light/ picks the light pair, any other value (dark, daltonized, ansi variants) the dark pair, and only an absent row falls back to the mid-tone `#5b84d6`, legible on both backgrounds for glyphs and labels. accent2 (the ruled lines): theme key `subtle` (fallback `inactive`) for the margin `│` and the `┄` rules, so the paper's lines follow the person's theme and sit fainter than dim text; the hex in the palette is only the mock page's rendering. bg2 (highlighter): hex `#3a3418` dark / `#fff2a8` light as `backgroundColor` on the body of the doing step row and on the current footer tab's label chip, drawn with `text` on top; when the theme row is absent no highlighter is drawn at all (bold and `✎` already mark the doing row, and the footer chip falls back to today's `[Overview]` brackets). The hotkey letter before each footer tab is the engine's own `hotkey` prefix (`1: `), shown in accent on the mock. success / warning / error: theme keys, unchanged meaning. Tone rule stated as a change: the health glyph takes the most severe open item (blocker → error, decision-only → warning, as in the sample); drift `~` is drawn on `text` bold (ink, not pencil) in the band and in the margin, so it sits between the warning `?` and the dim todo rows and is never read as decoration.

{bold}~{/} {accent2}│{/} commit 3f2a1bc not linked to a step                             {dim}3m{/}

otherTabs: Plan keeps the same page: every phase is a `▸`/`✓`/`□` margin glyph with a bold title and a `n/m` note at the right column; the fold indicator (`▾`/`▸`) is dropped from the phase Button's label, since fold state shows by whether step rows follow, and done phases, when unfolded, show their steps dimmed under them; the one doing row anywhere carries the highlighter. Log is a ledger through the same 5-cell frame: the margin holds `§` for a Ruling and is blank otherwise, the body starts with the time as its first 6 cells (`16:40 ` as today's padEnd(6)) followed by the entry, and Ruling bodies are warning-toned so they read as the notebook's rulings. Step details is a single page about one line: the step's glyph and title as the header row, then `status / note / commit / gate / agents / drift / asks` as 8-cell dim labels in the body column with values aligned after them, and its log lines in ledger form. Needs-you is the margin written large: each question is a `?` row with its `asked 16:05 · blocks B4` note, the `why` indented under it, options as `[ per seat (recommended) ] [ per workspace ]` buttons on one row, the text field beneath; answered items become `✓` rows with `Claude has it · 2m` in the right column.
glyphs: todo `□` (dim, an unticked box) · doing `✎` (accent ink, bold: the pen is on this line; the row also gets the bg2 highlighter) · done `✓` (success) · blocked `!` (error) · skipped `–` (dim) · current phase `▸` (accent; chips read `✓A ▸B □C` with ✓ success, ▸ accent, □ dim) · decision `?` (warning, bold) · blocker `!` (error, bold) · drift `~` (`text`, bold: ink, noticed but not asked) · health: `✎` working (accent), `!` needs you (warning when only decisions wait, error when a blocker does), `✗` gate red (error), `✓` finished (success) · meter cells: `■` filled (accent) and `□` empty (dim); in the band 10 cells rounded as today (7/18 → 4), in the pane one box per step (18 boxes for 18 steps, so the meter IS the checklist), falling back to 20 rounded cells above 24 steps · separators `·` dim · margin line `│` and section rules `┄` on `subtle`. States: finished reads as a page fully ticked (every margin glyph `✓`, no highlighter, the band `✓ 18/18 ■■■■■■■■■■ · 9e1d0aa 2m · took 3h12m` with no step and no counts); with nothing asked the top section is the `~ NOTICED` rule on `text` bold and its rows, and with nothing noticed either the section is omitted while the one-blank-row rhythm between header, PLAN and SIGNALS is kept; a band with no current step (between phases) shows glyph, count, meter and the trailing segments only, the pen absent. Every glyph is a width-1 BMP character; `✎` is U+270E (Dingbats, no emoji presentation). Nothing in the engine reports glyph coverage, so the pen is a `userConfig` toggle (pen glyph: `✎` or `●`, default `✎`) for a font without Dingbats.
spacingRules: Every row of the pane goes through one frame: cell 1 space, cell 2 the margin glyph, cell 3 space, cell 4 the margin line `│`, cell 5 space, body from cell 6. The right column (sha, agent + time + tool, elapsed, counts, `blocks B4`, `? D1`, and the PLAN chip strip) is right-aligned to end on cell 71 on every row; body text is clipped so at least 2 cells separate it from the note. Rules alone (`LABEL ┄┄┄`) and the highlighter band run to cell 72, one cell past the note column, so lines read as lines and text as text; on the PLAN rule the dashes stop 2 cells before the chips. Sections are separated by exactly one blank row that still carries the margin line (header → NEEDS YOU → PLAN → SIGNALS → footer); never two blanks, never zero. Section labels sit on the body column. SIGNALS labels share a width of 7 plus one space (`gate   `, `git    `, `ctx    `); the step-details labels share 8. Footer tabs are separated by 2 cells; each is the engine's `hotkey` prefix (`1: `) and the label, the current tab's label a highlighter chip with one space inside each end. In the band there is no margin line (a single row cannot stack one): the health glyph and a space, the count, the meter followed by two spaces, segments joined by ` · ` in dim, and the right counts keep the engine's 3-cell minimum gap plus 2 between `? 1` and `~ 1`. Never adjacent: a note and body text; a glyph and the margin line; two sections; a section label and a note column (labels never carry notes except the PLAN chips).
desktopNotes: Proportional fonts cannot stack `│` into a line or size `┄` to the width, so on desktop, VS Code and mobile the margin line and the rules are dropped and the frame is kept as layout: each row is a flex row of a fixed-width margin Box (width 3, the glyph centered) and a body Box (flexGrow) with the note pushed right by a flexGrow spacer, which aligns the right column without spaces. SIGNALS and step-details labels are a fixed-width Box (`width={8}`) on every surface, never space-padded text, so `gate` / `git` / `ctx` align in a proportional font too. Section labels become the ink-blue (or warning) uppercase label alone with marginTop 1, as the current non-mono code does. The highlighter band survives as the body Box's backgroundColor, the footer chip as a Text chip, and the one-box-per-step meter stays (geometric boxes are the same glyphs). In the two-column inline layout (width >= 96) the left column (PLAN) keeps the full frame with its margin line and the right column (NEEDS YOU, SIGNALS) uses glyph + space only, so the page has one ruled margin. On mobile the pane is one column, the footer wraps to two rows if needed, Input is replaced by the "Reply in chat" button, and nothing animates; the band is not drawn there anyway. VS Code has no band; the pane follows the desktop rules.

animation.idea: Things get written into the margin by hand: a margin glyph that changes inks in over three frames from its previous glyph instead of appearing. doing → done goes `✎` → `■` (dim) → `✓` (success); todo → done goes `□` → `■` (dim) → `✓`; a question raised goes `·` → `?` (dim) → `?` (warning, bold); the pen `✎` appears the same way when it moves to the next line, and the highlighter band simply moves with it on the state redraw. Nothing moves otherwise; the page rests.
animation.trigger: A step changing status (done, doing), a decision or blocker arriving, a phase becoming current. A gate passing does not animate: the SIGNALS gate row turns success on the redraw, and the band's health glyph changes on the ordinary state redraw too; the band's text is never animated.
animation.cadence: One-shot, 3 frames at ~120 ms each (about 360 ms), then static. Skipped entirely (the final frame is drawn at once) when a key was pressed in the last 2 s, when the pane is not visible, and on mobile and VS Code; on desktop the Svg frame is static.
animation.element: Client, on the terminal only: the pane is a row Box of ONE Client (width 5, height = the visible rows, props = the per-row list of {glyph, tone, changedAt}) beside a column of body rows; every body row is 1 cell high (truncate-end) so the margin and the bodies stay aligned, and the body rows with their Buttons are untouched. Svg (static final glyph) on desktop; none on mobile and VS Code.
animation.staticFrame: The resting state is exactly the mock: `✓` on done rows, `✎` on the doing row with its highlighter band, `?` in the margin of the question, `~` on the drift row, `□` on the rest.

feasibility: Everything in the mock is Box/Text/Button with theme keys or hex, except these points. (1) The doing row is a Button inside a Box with `backgroundColor`: a plain Button draws its label alone, so the band comes from the row Box; if the Button's own focus style fights the band, the fallback is `inverse` on the row Text with the Button label unstyled. (2) `✎` U+270E is width-1 and not an emoji, but a font without Dingbats coverage shows a tofu and the engine cannot detect that, so the pen glyph is a `userConfig` toggle (`✎` or `●`, default `✎`) that covers the doing glyph and the working health glyph. (3) Hex accents cannot follow the terminal theme on their own: the hooks module reads the `theme` row of `$.config.list()` (/light/ → light pair, else dark); when the row is absent the mid-tone ink `#5b84d6` is used for glyphs and labels and no highlighter is drawn (bold + `✎` mark the doing row, the footer falls back to `[Overview]`). (4) The margin line and rules are on the `subtle` theme key, so they need no theme detection. (5) The 18-box pane meter is drawn by `meter(done, total, total)` when total ≤ 24, else 20 cells rounded; the band keeps 10. (6) The right-column notes `? D1` (from `attention.blocks`), `sonnet 1m` on a todo step (a running agent linked to it) and `blocks B4` on a question row are all available in ViewData but are new behavior (see implementation notes). (7) Under ~56 columns the 5-cell margin frame is costly; below 48 the margin line is dropped (glyph + space only) and the right column collapses to the sha alone, as the band already does by dropping segments. (8) The footer renders through the engine's `hotkey` prefix, so each tab reads `1: Overview`; the mock draws exactly that, with the current label as the bg2 chip. (9) The ink-in animation is one Client of width 5 beside the body column (ClientProps has no overlay or z-order); the step rows beside it stay Buttons, so pressing is unaffected, and the Client draws the final glyph at once when the idle rules say so. (10) The band carries no `│`: it is today's segments with new glyphs and tones, so nothing new is drawn there.
implementationNotes:
- Glyph tables: `GLYPH` becomes todo `□`, doing `✎` (or `●` by the `pen` userConfig), done `✓`, blocked `!`, skipped `–`; `healthOf` returns the pen/success while working and `!` with warning for decisions only, error when a blocker waits; `chips()` uses `▸` for the current phase; `meter()` returns `■`/`□`, and `drawPane` passes `total` as the cell count when `total <= 24`, else 20. Band `~ n` segment drops its `warning` tone for `text` and stays bold; `? n` stays warning, `! n` error; the band's count takes the accent, the health segment is unchanged in shape.
- One `row(t, key, glyph, glyphTone, body, note, { highlight, dim })` helper draws every pane row: on the terminal it emits only the body Box (flexGrow, `backgroundColor` bg2 when `highlight`), a flexGrow spacer and the note Text clipped so the body keeps 2 cells from it, 1 row high (truncate-end), and pushes `{glyph, tone, changedAt}` onto the margin list that the single `MarginInk` Client (width 5, height = rows) draws beside the column; off the terminal, or below 48 columns, it emits a width-3 margin Box with the glyph instead. Header, needs, phase, step, loose-agent, signals, blank and footer rows all go through it; `rule()` draws the label (accent bold, or warning for NEEDS YOU, `text` for NOTICED) plus `┄` on `subtle`, and a blank `row` is emitted before every rule and before the footer.
- Row budget: today's `stepRows = budget - needsRows - signalRows - 3` further subtracts the 4 blank rows and the PLAN rule row; when rows are too few the blank rows survive and the steps fold into `+N more`, never the other way round; the two-column layout subtracts its own blanks the same way.
- New notes in the right column: `stepRow` shows a running linked agent (`model age [tool]`) for todo steps too, shows `? D1` (warning) when a decision's `blocks` names the step, and the sha otherwise; `needsBlock` gains a note column (`blocks B4` for decisions, age for drift) instead of the inline `3m ` prefix; `fullPlan` drops the `▾`/`▸` fold indicator from the phase label.
- Footer: Buttons keep `plain` labels and their `hotkey`, so the engine draws `1: Overview`; the current tab's label is a Text chip with `backgroundColor` bg2 (` Overview `), replacing the `[Overview]` brackets, and the Needs-you count is a warning Text chip; with no highlighter available the brackets stay.
- Colors: a `tones()` helper in the hooks module reads the `theme` row of `$.config.list()` once per session and returns `{ ink, highlighter: { bg, fg } | null }` (/light/ → light pair, else dark, absent row → mid-tone ink and `null` highlighter); `view.tsx` receives it in `ViewData` so the drawing stays pure.
- Animation: the `MarginInk` Client surface module is the pane's margin column; the hooks module records `changedAt` per step id and attention id, and the Client inks a glyph over 3 frames from its previous glyph when its change is younger than 400 ms and no key was pressed in the last 2 s; otherwise it draws the resting glyph. Desktop gets a static Svg of the glyph; mobile and VS Code get Text only.
- Tests: `bandSegments` width and drop order at 100/80/60 columns with the new glyphs; `meter` box counts (18-of-18 exact, 10 rounded); `healthOf` tone by severity; `ruleParts` with `┄`; the row budget keeps 4 blank rows at 12 rows; `tones()` picks light/dark/fallback from sample config rows; a snapshot of `textOf` unchanged (the Markdown form keeps the old glyphs for cloud sessions).
